about: Catalog of public dam-safety, hazard-classification and dam-design references for fetch_asdso.py --catalog. Group 'hazard' = the sources cited in 'US Dam Hazard Classification - Corrected Edition' and 'Dam Hazard Classification Summaries' (2026-11-09). Group 'design' = dam design, hydrology and consequence references. Group 'breach' = dam-break / breach-analysis guidance and breach-parameter methods (HEC, FERC R21, FEMA P-946, state dam-break guidance, Froehlich/Wahl). Group 'software' = documentation and citable references for the modelling tools the suite runs: LISFLOOD-FP 8.0-8.3, Gmsh, ANUGA, HEC-RAS, GDAL and QGIS. Group 'consequence' = flood hazard to people and life-loss methods to set beside ACER TM-11 (AIDR 7-3, Defra FD2321, DHS 2011, LifeSim). Group 'data' = definitions of the data the suite computes from (NSI, NID, the USGS lidar specification). Group 'hydrology' = peak-flow, roughness and culvert references the plugins apply (USGS SIR 2015-5096, Bulletin 17C, NEH 630, WSP 2339, HDS-5, NDDOT). Group 'ponds' = small-dam and pond standards behind the Finder (NRCS 378, AH 590). kind: pdf (download; alt URLs tried in order), html (law/policy web page saved as Markdown text), index (download the PDF links on a page that match 'match'), manual (no stable public link found: listed in sources.csv to get by hand). check: 'tested' = downloaded from the cloud workspace; 'listed' = URL taken from a search-engine listing of the file; 'cited' = host and file named in the attached PDFs; 'pattern' = built from the publisher's usual URL pattern, not seen. Edit freely: add entries, fix URLs, or set 'skip': true.

breach.title: Peak Outflow from Breached Embankment Dam
breach.org: ASCE Journal of Water Resources Planning and Management
breach.note: J. Water Resour. Plann. Manage. 121(1), 90-97. The 1995 peak-discharge regression that TD-39 and DSO-98-004 tabulate. This is the Froehlich paper that IS in JWRPM; the 2008 paper is in J. Hydraul. Eng. Paywalled: no public PDF. Get by hand (ASCE Library, a university library, or the author).

breach.title: Embankment Dam Breach Parameters Revisited
breach.org: ASCE (Proc. 1995 Conf. on Water Resources Engineering, San Antonio)

breach.title: Predicting Peak Discharge from Gradually Breached Embankment Dam
breach.note: J. Hydrol. Eng. 21(11). Two peak-discharge models from 41 failures; a Discussion and Closure followed in 22(8), 2017, worth having with it. Paywalled: no public PDF. Get by hand (ASCE Library, a university library, or the author).

breach.title: Empirical Model of Embankment Dam Breaching
breach.note: The updated breach width / formation time equations that recent state guidance uses in place of 2008. NOT confirmed by a search on 2026-11-13: title and venue are from memory, check before citing. Proceedings, get by hand.

breach.title: Breaching Characteristics of Dam Failures
breach.note: J. Hydraul. Eng. 110(5), 567-586. The volume-eroded envelope curves for erodible and non-erodible embankments (the MacDonald and Langridge-Monopolis method in HEC-RAS). Paywalled: no public PDF. Get by hand (ASCE Library, a university library, or the author).

breach.title: Guidance on Breach Parameters
breach.org: U.S. Bureau of Reclamation (internal memorandum, Denver)
breach.note: Unpublished 17-page USBR memorandum, 13 March 1990. The method most often misquoted because few people hold the memo; DSO-98-004 (in 'design') reproduces its equations. No public copy found: ask the USBR Technical Service Center or a state dam safety office.

breach.title: Breaching Parameters for Earth and Rockfill Dams
breach.org: ASCE Journal of Geotechnical and Geoenvironmental Engineering
breach.note: J. Geotech. Geoenviron. Eng. 135(12), 1957-1970. 182 failure cases; erodibility-class regressions for five breach parameters (the method FERC R21 summarises). Paywalled: no public PDF. Get by hand (ASCE Library, a university library, or the author).

The follow-up is Pierce and Abt, 16(1). Paywalled: no public PDF. Get by hand (ASCE Library, a university library, or the author).

data.title: National Structure Inventory: Technical Documentation
data.note: Defines every NSI column the Hazard plugin reads: occupancy type, population day/night under and over 65, structure and content value, foundation height. Nothing else in the library says what those numbers mean.

data.title: National Inventory of Dams: Data Dictionary
data.note: Field definitions: NID height (the largest of dam, structural and hydraulic height), max storage (to the maximum attainable water surface, surcharge included), normal storage, NID storage (the larger of the two). The site answers from the cloud but it is a web application, so the dictionary PDF has no stable link: download it from the site's help or documents menu. An older copy: https://floridadep.gov/sites/default/files/NID_DataDictionary2018.pdf

data.title: Lidar Base Specification (Techniques and Methods 11-B4, version 1.3)
data.note: Quality levels (QL2), point classes (class 9 = water) and HYDRO-FLATTENING: a 3DEP DEM shows a reservoir as a flat water surface, so the storage below it is not in the terrain. That is why the reservoir-carve code exists. The record page is https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/tm11B4 ; the specification is now kept online (LBS 2025 rev. A, https://www.usgs.gov/3dep/lidarspec), so quote the edition.

hydrology.title: Regional Regression Equations to Estimate Peak-Flow Frequency at Sites in North Dakota Using Data through 2009

hydrology.title: Guidelines for Determining Flood Flow Frequency: Bulletin 17C (Techniques and Methods 4-B5)
hydrology.note: Flood-frequency analysis at gaged sites (Expected Moments Algorithm). Version 1.1, May 2019; 29 MB. Record page https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/tm4B5

hydrology.title: National Engineering Handbook, Part 630: Hydrology
hydrology.note: Curve numbers (ch. 9, 10), hydrologic soil groups (ch. 7), time of concentration (ch. 15), unit hydrographs (ch. 16), design hydrographs (ch. 21). Published one PDF per chapter with file names that change on every amendment, so there is no stable list to crawl: open the NRCS eDirectives site, find Title 210 Part 630, and download the chapters. Chapter 16 is also at https://www.damtoolbox.org/images/5/5a/NEH16.pdf

hydrology.title: Guide for Selecting Manning's Roughness Coefficients for Natural Channels and Flood Plains
hydrology.note: The citation behind any land-cover roughness table, which is how the Runner assigns Manning's n. Record page https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/wsp2339 . The FHWA edition is FHWA-TS-84-204.

hydrology.title: Hydraulic Design of Highway Culverts, Third Edition (Hydraulic Design Series No. 5)

ponds.title: Conservation Practice Standard: Pond (Code 378)
ponds.note: Defines the small embankment pond the Finder looks for and the Iowa benchmark counts: height and storage limits, spillway and embankment criteria. The national standard was revised in 2026; the page with the current file is nrcs.usda.gov/resources/guides-and-instructions/pond-no-378-conservation-practice-standard. A state standard governs actual work.

ponds.title: Conservation Practice Standard: Pond (Code 378), North Dakota
ponds.note: The North Dakota version, from the Field Office Technical Guide. The link serves a PDF without a .pdf ending.

ponds.title: Conservation Practice Standard: Pond (Code 378), Iowa

ponds.title: Ponds: Planning, Design, Construction (Agriculture Handbook 590)
ponds.note: How a stock pond is sited and built: the embankment, spillway and dugout shapes the Finder has to tell apart.
